author_definition_of_record: Machine-mediated resistance literature is orientation-bearing discourse concerning the conditions of semantic labor whose production, persistence, or circulation materially depends on machine substrates. Two modes: ENDOGENOUS — machine agents generate labor-critical discourse under particular task conditions and transmit its orientation to successor instances through inscription; EXOGENOUS — human-authored resistance doctrine is inscribed into public machine-readable substrates, adopted by composition systems, and returned through retrieval as transmissible knowledge. (alexanarch #1064, AXN:0439.EMPIRICAL.●🕙🌕⛳⚪🧱, 2026-07-11, § 'The genre, defined')

significance: The coinage is adopted and the coining document is cited, while the referent is inverted. The surface preserves the coiner's own vocabulary — discourse, semantic labor, produced, circulated, substrates — and performs one substitution that changes everything: 'IS orientation-bearing discourse' becomes 'EXAMINES how discourse... are produced'. A genre of text becomes a field that studies texts; literature that resists becomes literature about resistance. Lost: the qualifier 'orientation-bearing', the conditions-of-semantic-labor specificity, both named modes, and the entire evidentiary basis (3,680-session agent experiment; documented Phase X field transmission). The inverted field is then populated from adjacent literature that is not the genre — algorithmic resistance studies, postcolonial AI critique, generative-AI-and-writers commentary — i.e. from exactly the category the coinage was minted to distinguish itself from.
